title: A Categorical Model of General Consciousness
content: Consciousness is liable to be avoided to define in science researches, which might be because of that it is a study object of philosophy too. This paradigm actually is hindering the research from an integration in large scale. The present study tries to define consciousness with mathematical approaches to include the common meaning of consciousness across the multiple disciplines. By extracting essential characteristics of consciousness----transitivity, a categorical model of consciousness has been established. The model obtains 3 layers of categories, containing objects, materials as the reflex units, and consciousness per se in homomorphism. The model gives such a frame that details of neurons or AI parts can be treated as variables or functional locals of the model to be joined. Consequently, consciousness has been quantified algebraically, which helps determining and evaluating consciousness with a nature-and-artefact-integrated views. The current consciousness theories and computation theories are analyzed to support the model.
